memo.verdict: PARK, medium conviction. The memo recommends placing EVK-DE on the monitored watchlist with a quarterly review cadence rather than progressing it to Early-Stage Assessment. The park is struck on entry point and competitive structure, explicitly not on management quality, restructuring credibility or balance sheet, all of which the memo rates at or above the peer median. The memo adopts the Risks report's own stage-progression verdict in full. Risks report §14 states the investor should "let the idea sit" rather than progressing it into a concentrated long position, and that "the investment case must be put on hold until Chinese capacity additions are fully digested by global markets". The memo states its evidence does not beat that verdict, it corroborates it from four independent directions: the entry multiple, the setup sweep, the thematic overlay and the value-chain read. Named re-activation triggers, three: (1) Chinese methionine capacity additions digested, specifically the Liben Crop 100 kilotonnes and Adisseo 150 kilotonnes lines commissioned and running with their price effect visible in Asian spot rather than forecast, with an Asian methionine spot trigger of EUR 2.40 per kilogram for an immediate pre-mortem re-run; (2) a forward multiple back in the bottom quartile of its own range from the current 68th percentile; (3) evidence that the ex-methionine business grows at or above specialty peers.
case: The memo's argument for the park runs in five steps.

Step one, the change forces are real and are the strongest in the peer set. E1.RA1 grades B. Corporate hierarchy compresses from ten management levels to a maximum of six by end-2026, with the median span of control widening from 1:4 to 1:7. The entire divisional management layer was eliminated on 1 April 2025 and fourteen legacy business lines consolidated into Custom Solutions and Advanced Technologies. The 2025 Capital Markets Day committed to EUR 1bn of incremental adjusted EBITDA by 2027 against a 2023 baseline and an 11% return on capital employed, now embedded in executive pay at a 40% long-term-incentive weighting. Christian Kullmann was extended to 2030 and Michael Rauch appointed chief financial officer effective 1 May 2026, ending an eight-month vacancy after Maike Schuh's sudden September 2025 resignation. The memo's peer anchor: Croda's activist-driven GBP 100m programme and Clariant's CHF 80m programme are both smaller in relative scale than a 6,000-role, 10%-of-workforce cut.

Step two, the base those forces act on is the weakest in the peer set. E1.RA2 grades D and fails four of five tests. Return on capital employed of 6.10% sits below a broker-estimated cost of capital of 6.70% to 7.60%, with economic value added of minus EUR 543m. R&D intensity holds at 3.00% of sales, EUR 418m absolute and down 9.00% year on year, against DSM-Firmenich at 7.00% and EUR 657m. Guidance delivery is repeatedly incongruent: FY23 guidance cut from EUR 2.1bn-EUR 2.4bn to EUR 1.6bn-EUR 1.8bn with EUR 1,656m delivered near the lower end; a second cut in September 2025 from EUR 2.0bn-EUR 2.3bn to around EUR 1.9bn; the EUR 2.7bn 2027 EBITDA target implicitly abandoned. Sales fell from EUR 18,488m in 2022 to EUR 15,267m in 2023, EUR 15,157m in 2024 and EUR 14,069m in 2025, which the memo calls a three-year contraction rather than a cycle trough. An expert call states the infrastructure group generates nearly USD 2bn of sales but only USD 20m of EBITDA, roughly a 1.00% margin.
counter_case: The Risks report's own recommendation, quoted by the memo, agrees with the park rather than opposing it. Risks report §14: the investor should "let the idea sit" rather than progressing it into a concentrated long position, and "the investment case must be put on hold until Chinese capacity additions are fully digested by global markets". The aggregated failure probability is stated as high-to-medium. The analysis of competing hypotheses crowns the FALSE FRIEND profile with zero hard inconsistencies across all fifteen assessed indicators, against eight for the bull thesis and two for the bear thesis. The memo goes further than the Risks report in one respect and is more generous in another: it adds that two of the six acceptable setup archetypes fail on the same entry-point test, making it a structural entry problem rather than a patience problem, while rating the underlying restructuring higher than the Risks report's framing implies, at B on the corporate-change archetype.

The strongest opposing argument the memo carried against its own park verdict, stated in the memo's Element E8 counter-view: a B on the corporate-change archetype should carry Element E8 higher than D. The corporate-change setup is the archetype Viewforth most often buys, and Evonik's version is unusually broad, at 6,000 roles, ten layers to six, fourteen business lines to two segments and a rebuilt incentive structure. The memo rejects it on the ground that the two negative guardrails are guardrails, not weights, and an F on the false-friend guardrail cannot be averaged away by a strong fit elsewhere, particularly when the Risks report reached the same conclusion independently.
triggers: Re-activation trigger one, capacity digestion. Re-open when the Liben Crop 100 kilotonnes and Adisseo 150 kilotonnes lines are commissioned and running and their price effect is visible in Asian spot rather than forecast. The observable is accelerating exports of solid and liquid methionine from Chinese ports, which the Risks report names as the leading indicator. The threshold is Asian methionine spot below EUR 2.40 per kilogram, the level the Risks report names for an immediate pre-mortem re-run. Sequential spread deflation in Asia is named as the key early warning of portfolio stress.

Re-activation trigger two, multiple reset. A forward multiple back in the bottom quartile of its own range, from the current 68th percentile. The memo's reason for naming this specific condition: both Element E8 required attribute five and required attribute six require a bottom-quartile multiple, and both fail today on that limb plus competitive behaviour.

Re-activation trigger three, the base business. Evidence that the ex-methionine business grows at or above specialty peers, testing the Jefferies claim that it structurally does not. The observable is Custom Solutions organic sales growth against the 7.00% recorded in the second quarter of 2026, stripped of amino acid pricing.

Two memo-level downstream actions, both owned by Watson. Action one: re-test the case on publication of the third-quarter 2026 result, specifically the ex-methionine organic growth rate and the second-half methionine spread roll-off against the "peak quarter" guidance. Action two: set a standing monitor on Asian methionine spot pricing with a EUR 2.40 per kilogram trigger and on Chinese port export volumes, reporting into the weekly change note.

Three questions the memo records as held rather than answered, for the re-open. Question one: the EUR 1bn EBITDA bridge decomposed into its three stated return-on-capital buckets, at three percentage points from project ramp-up, one from immediate-return capex and four from restructuring. Question two: net rather than gross Tailor Made retention against the 7.00% German chemical wage settlement, given the very low historical net retention Jefferies records on cost-cutting exercises. Question three: the C4 Oxeno transaction value and balance-sheet relief, which the Key-Question research names as an open data gap.

Element-level downstream actions carried. Element E1: rebuild the EUR 1bn EBITDA bridge from its three stated return-on-capital buckets; track the ex-methionine organic growth rate separately from group. Element E5: re-score against Thematics 1 to 3 once they are substantively re-reviewed, since the thematics file's own header marks them carried forward from 16 April 2026 without re-review; size the data-centre immersion cooling and semiconductor hydrogen peroxide exposures in revenue terms, which no source currently does. Element E7: re-test the perimeter guardrail on completion of the C4 Oxeno divestment, which alone removes EUR 1.9bn of sales; test net rather than gross Tailor Made retention using personnel expense per employee as the tracking variable. Element E8: re-run the trough-on-trough nine-condition sweep after Chinese capacity commissions, since three of the failing conditions turn on competitor behaviour the capacity wave itself will resolve; track the corporate-change archetype separately from the spread using Tailor Made net savings per quarter and ex-methionine segment EBITDA. Element E11: set a standing monitor on Chinese methionine export volumes from Chinese ports; track the Mobile cash-cost advantage against landed Chinese cost once the methylmercaptan facility completes in 2026, which the memo names as the one variable that could lift the Element.
